title: Smart Path Resolver for precision heterogeneity with online accuracy checks
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime component (Smart Path Resolver, SPR) that chooses a per-request/per-layer execution path across FP16/FP8/INT8 kernels using stored quantization profiles and lightweight online accuracy checks. The SPR should maximize cost savings from lower-precision paths while bounding accuracy regressions via sampled validation and fast micro-calibration.

Scope and requirements:
- Input: model metadata contains a set of quantization profiles (per-layer FP8/INT8 scales, error estimates, per-op compatibility flags) produced by offline calibration.
- Runtime behavior: for each incoming request, SPR computes a path plan (sequence of kernel choices) using: (a) static profile heuristics (expected error & latency), (b) recent online telemetry (per-customer distribution shift), and (c) policy constraints (SLO, cost budget, customer tier).
- Online validation: sample ~1-5% of requests to run a secondary verification pass (either re-run last N tokens at FP16 or compute logit-delta estimates) and maintain a rolling accuracy score per model + profile. If rolling score crosses threshold, automatically (i) trigger fallback to safer path for subsequent requests, and (ii) schedule a lightweight micro-calibration job.
- Micro-calibration: fast per-batch recalibration that re-estimates scale/zero values on a handful of recent tokens to correct distribution shift without blocking requests. If micro-calibration fails to bring accuracy within threshold, escalate to full offline calibration pipeline.
- Fallbacks & safety: per-request and per-model fallback policies, with priority for high-tier customers and requests marked as high-accuracy. SPR must support deterministic fallback to FP16 and to a cached KV-primed FP16 path for very low latency needs.

Acceptance criteria:
- SPR chooses mixed-precision path and logs chosen kernels + estimated errors for every request.
- Online checks detect a simulated distribution drift (bench harness) and trigger fallback within N=500 requests for p95 latency below 2x baseline and accuracy delta within policy.
- End-to-end benchmarks on Llama-2-70B and a curated set of customer-like prompts show >=35% token-cost reduction vs always-FP16 while keeping mean logit-gap < 0.015 on eval set.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Use existing quant-profile schemas from offline calibrator (conform to storage format in /confluence/calibration-spec). Keep profile versioning in model manifest.
- Runtime cost model needs to be extended to include FP8/INT8 effective token cost and added micro-calibration overhead.
- Telemetry: add a lightweight metric "spr.rolling_accuracy" and sample-level logs for any fallback events. Keep privacy-safe (no full-prompt storage).
- Edge cases: for models with non-uniform per-layer sensitivity (attention vs FF layers), SPR should allow per-layer forced modes configured by model owner.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Extra runtime decision logic adds ~1-3ms overhead per request; mitigate by caching path plans for common prompt shapes and batched resolution.
- False negatives in online check could allow silent quality regressions; mitigate by conservatively tuning sampling rate and thresholds for public release.
- Micro-calibration accuracy depends on sampled tokens; if customers use adversarial prompts, fallback to safer path faster.

Next steps and deliverables:
1) Spike (this ticket) to implement a prototype SPR in the runtime test harness (deadline 2025-02-21). Deliverable: prototype that selects between FP16 and FP8 paths and performs one-line online logit-delta check. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7892 (WIP).
2) Integrate micro-calibration library: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAL/Micro-Calibration-Design (draft).
3) Bench: run mixed-precision cost/accuracy sweep with eval-set-2025 and produce dashboard (console-2025.02).
4) PM review and release gating: add config flags in Dedicated and Private for SPR opt-in, document default behavior for Hosted customers.
